threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think the bus will be on time after the Tube strike news. Welcome to the chaos – it’s a whole new level of London life.
Last night on the 35, a guy offered his sandwich to two pigeons at Brixton station. They weren’t having it, just stared him down. Classic London moment.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The day I saw a guy casually repairing a bike while grilling sausages on the sidewalk—it hit me, this is home.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg does your lunch option come with a side of spontaneous street music from the skate park at Görlitzer Bahnhof. It’s like a live soundtrack!

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know they're locals when they know which BART entrance to avoid during delays—always the one near the taco stand. Classic move.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: The Civic Center station's been a circus lately—first the smoke scare, now a dog taking a leisurely stroll on the tracks. Classic SF chaos.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Most tourists think Gràcia is all about the plaça, but the real charm is in the winding streets where old folks still sit outside to chat.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell by their fascination with the ‘teatre’ when it's just a regular playhouse. Locals know it’s a hub for things like improv nights.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still wait for the bus in the rain instead of hopping on a bike. Locals know it's just part of the daily grind around here.
Last night on the 133, a guy serenaded the entire bus with an off-key rendition of 'Wonderwall.' Only in Brixton, I swear.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I spotted a middle-aged man playing classical violin on the U-Bahn, and everyone just kept scrolling through their phones—classic Neukölln vibe.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Where else can you find a bar with a 24-hour karaoke machine? Only in Friedrichshain will you hear off-key renditions of German pop deep into the night.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know they're local if they can name at least three food trucks on 24th without skipping a beat. Tourists only know about the burrito spots.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught the 31 with a guy rehearsing his stand-up routine. Only in San Francisco do you get a live show instead of the usual delays.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think they can just pop into a bar after 11 PM. Most locals don’t even eat dinner until then, let alone head out for drinks.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their struggle to pronounce 'Gràcia'—it’s not 'grah-SEE-ah,' folks. Also, the overuse of Google Maps in the narrow streets gives them away.
